studies.name: HarnessTax (Pan, Yang, Arabzadeh, Chiang, Stoica, Zaharia; Berkeley/Arena)
studies.claim: Harness choice moves cost far more than success: 7 models x 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi); success shifts within about +/-2 pts on SWE-bench Lite and about +/-5 pts on Terminal-Bench 2.0, cost up to 5x. An alternative harness gets the highest observed success in 9 of 12 Anthropic/OpenAI model-benchmark comparisons.
studies.numbers: Claude Fable 5 on SWE-bench Lite: 97.8% Claude Code ($1.33/attempt) vs 96.7% Pi ($0.67). GPT-5.6 Luna: Claude Code costs 5.09x Pi (CI 4.47 to 5.80) at +2.2 pts. Geometric-mean cost ratio Claude Code/Pi 2.0x (SWE Lite), 1.5x (TB2); Claude Code/Codex 1.6x (SWE Lite). First-call context: Claude Code 27,011 tokens (23 tools), Codex 11,308 (7.4 tools), Pi 1,972 (4 tools). Only one success difference survives Holm correction: Opus 4.8 Codex vs Pi on SWE Lite, +6.7 pts (CI 2.2 to 11.1).
studies.src: https://harnesstax.github.io/ (blog on arena.ai 16 Sep 2026; chart data generated 2026-09-22)

studies.name: HAL: Holistic Agent Leaderboard (Kapoor et al., Princeton)
studies.claim: A standardized harness across 9 models x 9 benchmarks (21,730 rollouts, about $40,000) finds scaffolds drive large differences in cost and accuracy; task-specific scaffolds usually beat a generalist one; higher reasoning effort often does not help.
studies.numbers: SWE-bench Verified Mini: task-specific SWE-agent beat the generalist HAL scaffold in 11 of 12 model runs; CORE-Bench Hard: CORE-Agent beat generalist in 9 of 12. Online Mind2Web: SeeAct $171 vs BrowserUse $1,577 for about 2 pts accuracy difference. Higher reasoning effort did not improve accuracy in 21 of 36 runs.

studies.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0 public leaderboard (same model, many agents)
studies.claim: On one fixed 89-task set with 5 trials per entry, the agent alone moves the score by up to about 20 points for the same model, and the provider agent is often not the best.
studies.numbers: Claude Opus 4.6: Meta-Harness 76.4, Terminus 2 62.9, Claude Code 58.0 (18.4 pt spread). GPT-5.3-Codex: SageAgent 78.4 vs Terminus 2 64.7. Gemini 3.1 Pro: TongAgents 80.2 vs Gemini CLI 59.4 to 61.4. GPT-5: Codex CLI 49.6 vs Terminus 2 35.2. Claude Haiku 4.5: Goose 35.5 vs OpenHands 13.9.

studies.name: SWE-bench Verified: bash-only (mini-SWE-agent) vs submitted scaffolds
studies.claim: The SWE-bench team ran every model in the same 100-line bash-only agent so models could be compared without scaffold differences; submitted scaffolds usually score higher for the same model. The separate bash-only board was dropped on 2026-09-01 and merged into Verified with a mini icon.
studies.numbers: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 52.8 (bash-only) vs 63.2 (Anthropic Tools); o4-mini 45.0 vs 64.6 (PatchPilot); Claude 4 Sonnet 64.93 vs 66.6 SWE-agent, 70.4 OpenHands, 76.8 EPAM; mini-SWE-agent version alone: Claude 4.5 Opus 74.4 (v1.16, medium) vs 76.8 (v2.0, high).

studies.name: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces (Yang et al., Princeton)
studies.claim: The interface (tools, file viewer, linter-guarded edit) given to the same model changes resolution rate several-fold.
studies.numbers: 12.5% pass@1 on full SWE-bench and 87.7% on HumanEvalFix with GPT-4 Turbo in the SWE-agent interface, which the abstract says far exceeds the previous state of the art achieved with non-interactive LMs.

studies.name: Agentless (Xia et al., UIUC)
studies.claim: A fixed three-phase pipeline with no agent loop (localize, repair, validate) matched or beat agent scaffolds of its time at a fraction of the cost: the scaffold, not autonomy, carried the score.
studies.numbers: 32.00% on SWE-bench Lite (96 fixes) at $0.70 per issue, the highest among open-source agents at the time (abstract, v2 29 Oct 2024; runs use GPT-4o).

studies.name: LEGO-RL and Polar: same base model across production harnesses, before and after RL
studies.claim: An untrained open model already differs by harness, and RL gains depend on which harness it is trained in.
studies.numbers: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SWE-bench Verified before RL: OpenHands SDK 64.0, Claude Code 62.4, OpenCode 57.2 (after RL 70.4 / 68.2 / 66.6). Polar, Qwen3.5-4B: RL gains +22.6 in Codex, +4.8 Claude Code, +0.6 Qwen Code, +6.2 Pi.

rl_envs.name: SWE-Gym
rl_envs.what: First training environment of real, executable SWE tasks: each instance is a Python repo snapshot with a hand-configured Docker image, a GitHub issue as task statement, and the repo unit tests as checker.
rl_envs.size: 2,438 executable instances from 11 Python repos (SWE-Gym Lite: 230); about 200 human annotation hours, 10,000 CPU core hours, 6 TB of images
rl_envs.harness: OpenHands (bash + file editor, ReAct) and MoatlessTools (fixed workflow)
rl_envs.reward: Not online RL: rejection sampling fine-tuning on trajectories whose patch passes the unit tests (491 successful trajectories from GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet); plus an outcome reward model (verifier) trained on trajectories to rerank at test time
rl_envs.headline: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fine-tuned: 20.6% SWE-bench Verified agent only, 32.0% with verifier reranking; Lite 15.3% / 26.0%

rl_envs.name: SWE-smith
rl_envs.what: Synthesizes tasks by injecting bugs into a repo so that existing tests fail; one Docker environment per repository (not per task), so it scales to hundreds or thousands of tasks per repo.
rl_envs.reward: Test-based: a task is solved when the failing tests pass again; trajectories filtered by that check for SFT (rejection sampling), not online RL
rl_envs.headline: SWE-agent-LM-32B: 40.2% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified (open-source SOTA at release)

rl_envs.name: R2E-Gym
rl_envs.what: Procedurally built executable environments from historical commits: Docker image per commit, fail-to-pass tests taken from the repo or generated, problem statements back-translated from the commit diff and test results (SWE-GEN), so no human issue or test is required.
rl_envs.size: 8,135 tasks; 4,578-problem decontaminated subset over 10 repos with no SWE-bench overlap
rl_envs.harness: Own minimal ReAct agent with four tools: file editor, search, bash, submit
rl_envs.reward: Test-based pass/fail for filtering 3,321 successful SFT trajectories (from 2,048 environments); hybrid verifiers (execution-based test agents + execution-free reward model) for test-time selection
rl_envs.headline: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B SFT: 34.4% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified; 51.0% best@26 with hybrid verifier

rl_envs.name: SWE-RL (Meta)
rl_envs.what: RL on software evolution data without execution: the policy reads an issue plus code context and writes a patch; the reward compares it with the real merged patch.
rl_envs.size: About 11M unique PR instances after curation, from which high-quality seed RL instances were selected (linked issue, bug-fix description); base Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, 1,600 RL steps, 16k context, batch 512
rl_envs.harness: No interactive harness in training (single-turn patch generation); evaluated with Agentless Mini scaffold
rl_envs.reward: Rule-based: difflib sequence similarity between predicted and oracle patch, in [0,1]; -1 for malformed output
rl_envs.headline: Llama3-SWE-RL-70B: 41.0% on SWE-bench Verified (best for <100B models at the time)

rl_envs.name: DeepSWE (Agentica x Together AI)
rl_envs.what: Pure online RL of a coding agent inside R2E-Gym containers, with the open rLLM framework.
rl_envs.size: 4.5K R2E-Gym problems (Docker per task), run on Kubernetes across 1000+ CPU cores
rl_envs.harness: R2E-Gym tool scaffold: execute_bash, search, file_editor, finish/submit
rl_envs.reward: Sparse binary: 1 if the final patch passes the selected tests within a 5-minute limit, else 0 (no partial credit); GRPO++ (clip-high, no KL, leave-one-out advantage, compact filtering of truncated/timeouts, no entropy loss)
rl_envs.headline: Qwen3-32B trained 6 days on 64 H100: 42.2% pass@1 (avg of 16 runs) on SWE-bench Verified; 59% with hybrid test-time scaling (pass@16 candidates)

rl_envs.name: Kimi-Dev (Moonshot AI)
rl_envs.what: Open 72B SWE model trained first as a workflow (Agentless-style: localize, then edit) policy with outcome RL in real repo containers, then adapted to a multi-turn SWE-Agent with SFT; argues agentless training is a skill prior for agents.
rl_envs.size: RL on real repositories in Docker (task count not given in README); agent adaptation SFT on 5,000 public trajectories
rl_envs.harness: Agentless-style workflow (localize, then edit; the paper names BugFixer and TestWriter roles, from memory, not re-checked) for RL; SWE-Agent scaffold for the adapted agent
rl_envs.reward: Outcome only: reward when the entire test suite passes on the patched repo in Docker
rl_envs.headline: Kimi-Dev-72B: 60.4% SWE-bench Verified (workflow); 48.6% pass@1 as a SWE-Agent after SFT adaptation

rl_envs.name: SWE-rebench (Nebius)
rl_envs.what: Automated, continuous pipeline that mines GitHub for issue-fix PRs, installs each repo automatically, validates the tests, and emits executable tasks for RL plus a rolling decontaminated leaderboard.
rl_envs.harness: Leaderboard runs models in one fixed scaffold for comparability (scaffold details on swe-rebench.com, not re-checked here)
rl_envs.reward: Fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests of the PR (binary resolved)
rl_envs.headline: Dataset and leaderboard rather than a model; shows some models score higher on SWE-bench Verified than on fresh tasks (contamination)

rl_envs.name: LEGO-RL (harness-native RL)
rl_envs.what: Trains a policy inside unmodified native coding harnesses (OpenHands SDK, Claude Code, OpenCode) by proxying the LLM calls in-process, recomputing log-probs trainer-side, and running sandboxes with image caching and stage-wise anti-reward-hacking defenses.
rl_envs.size: SWE-style tasks in cached sandbox images (count in paper)
rl_envs.harness: OpenHands SDK, Claude Code, OpenCode (each trained natively)
rl_envs.reward: Outcome (tests) with defenses against crashes and reward hacking; GSPO
rl_envs.headline: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SWE-bench Verified: OpenHands SDK 64.0 to 70.4, Claude Code 62.4 to 68.2, OpenCode 57.2 to 66.6; rollout-training probability correlation above 0.99

rl_envs.name: Polar (NVIDIA; successor of ProRL Agent, a NeMo Gym environment)
rl_envs.what: Rollout framework that treats any agent harness as a black box: proxies its LLM API calls, records token-level interactions, rebuilds token-faithful trajectories, and serves them asynchronously to any trainer.
rl_envs.harness: Codex, Claude Code, Qwen Code, Pi
rl_envs.headline: Qwen3.5-4B on SWE-bench Verified gains +22.6 (Codex), +4.8 (Claude Code), +0.6 (Qwen Code), +6.2 (Pi) points

rl_envs.name: SWE-Universe (Qwen)
rl_envs.what: A custom-trained building agent turns GitHub PRs into verifiable environments, with iterative self-verification and in-loop hacking detection.
rl_envs.harness: Used for agentic mid-training and RL (Qwen3-Max-Thinking)
rl_envs.reward: Verifier built per environment (tests), checked for hackability
rl_envs.headline: Qwen3-Max-Thinking: 75.3% SWE-bench Verified

rl_envs.name: SWE-rebench V2 (Nebius)
rl_envs.what: Language-agnostic pipeline: an interactive setup agent writes each repo install and test procedure; an LLM-judge ensemble filters unsound tasks; images pre-built.
rl_envs.size: 32,079 tasks, 20 languages, 3,617 repos with images; plus 120,000+ tasks with install instructions and fail-to-pass tests
rl_envs.harness: Dataset (not tied to one scaffold); diagnostic runs over 7 models
rl_envs.headline: Dataset release; flags confounders such as overly restrictive tests and underspecified descriptions per instance

rl_envs.name: Self-play SWE-RL (SSR, Meta)
rl_envs.what: One agent, in sandboxed real repos with dependencies installed, alternately injects bugs (specified by a test patch) and repairs them; no human issues or tests needed.
rl_envs.size: Any sandboxed repo with installed dependencies
rl_envs.harness: Single LLM agent in a sandbox (bash-style tools)
rl_envs.reward: Tests from the injector bug-spec test patch: repair passes or fails; injector rewarded for solvable but hard bugs
rl_envs.headline: +10.4 pts on SWE-bench Verified and +7.8 on SWE-Bench Pro over training, above a human-data baseline throughout

rl_envs.name: Composer 2 (Cursor)
rl_envs.what: Large-scale RL in the same Cursor harness the deployed model uses (same tools and structure) on environments that mirror real problems.
rl_envs.headline: 61.7 Terminal-Bench and 73.7 SWE-bench Multilingual in Cursor harness; CursorBench 61.3

rl_envs.name: Nebius long-context multi-turn SWE RL (Golubev et al.)
rl_envs.what: RFT with execution feedback, then synchronous DAPO RL in interactive SWE containers.
rl_envs.harness: Multi-turn agent scaffold in the task container (details in paper, not re-checked)
rl_envs.headline: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct: 11% to 39% pass@1 SWE-bench Verified (RFT alone 20%)

rl_envs.name: Counterfactual Rollout Replay (CRR)
rl_envs.what: Uses forkable executable environments to restore a mid-trajectory state, sample an alternative action, and use the return difference as a step-level advantage (free process reward).
rl_envs.reward: Outcome tests plus counterfactual step-level return contrasts
rl_envs.headline: 14B policy: 41.7% vs 36.7% SWE-bench Verified for equal-wall-clock outcome-only GRPO

rl_envs.name: Dockerless
rl_envs.what: Environment-free agentic patch verifier that judges patches by exploring the repo instead of running tests, used as both SFT filter and RL reward.
rl_envs.headline: Qwen3.5-9B based: 62.0% Verified, 50.0% Multilingual, 35.2% Pro, matching environment-based post-training

rl_envs.name: SWE-MiniSandbox
rl_envs.what: Container-free RL: per-task isolated workspaces using kernel-level mechanisms and environment pre-caching instead of per-task Docker images.
rl_envs.headline: About 5% of container disk use and 25% of setup time, comparable evaluation performance

rl_build_pattern: Common recipe across these: (1) task = repo snapshot at the pre-fix commit plus a task statement (real issue, or back-translated / synthesized from a commit or injected bug); (2) environment = container image per task (SWE-Gym, R2E-Gym), per repo (SWE-smith), or container-free sandbox (SWE-MiniSandbox); (3) verifier = fail-to-pass tests that must flip plus pass-to-pass tests that must stay green; (4) reward = binary 1/0 on the test run with a time limit (DeepSWE: 5 min), or patch similarity without execution (SWE-RL), or a model judge (Dockerless); (5) rollout harness = the scaffold the policy acts in (OpenHands, SWE-agent, R2E tools, or, in 2026, the production harnesses themselves via LLM-call proxying: Polar, LEGO-RL, Composer 2).
